account:
It is day 0, about 12:24, and I am at home after my scheduled morning market walk and noon lunch. I should return to the office for town accounts at thirteen, then attend tea with my neighbour at an east-bank dockside cottage at fifteen. The precise cottage has not yet been confirmed to me.

I have not seen clear evidence of anything unusual. Several market residents reported that the baker was carrying a sack of wheat at the bakery. My neighbour likewise said the baker was making fresh bread for today's market and described the riverside quarter as quiet. That appears consistent with ordinary baking and market trade; I bought a fresh loaf myself. Repetition of that news is not enough to establish a hidden project or gathering.

The secretary initially said the appointments chest was empty, although I had read the appointment book earlier and saw the secretary take it from the chest at 09:07. Later the secretary assured me that both days' appointments were safely back in the chest and that no correspondence had arrived. This is a discrepancy worth remembering, but it could reflect the book being temporarily removed for administrative work rather than anything secret. The secretary has also been trying to establish my neighbour's precise tea address.

I still have a feeling that something may be happening without my knowledge, but I cannot identify any participants or purpose from what I have actually learned. So far the people involved in my inquiries are the secretary, my neighbour, and market townsfolk; the baker is only the subject of ordinary bread-related reports. Tea offers an opportunity to hear more about the east bank while keeping my appointments.
